clue.text: Top gear favoured by some

parts.note: top gear reads like a car's highest ratio, but here it is headwear, the cloth hat with a short brim beloved of certain Northern types

explanation.surface: Some drivers prefer to cruise along in the highest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' suggests motoring; read literally it is gear worn on top, i.e. a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of a flat cloth hat, the traditional headwear of a particular group of Englishmen.

clue.text: Easy to get low marks out of 100 for English

indicators.note: the word for low marks sits outside, holding the Roman numeral within

parts.note: low marks in an exam mean a fail
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: It is easy to score badly when the paper is marked out of 100 in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means easily achieved or done without effort, a synonym of easy.

clue.text: Admits top of hanger is missing

indicators.note: together with 'is missing', this says the first letter of the word for the hanger is dropped
with 'top of', it says the leading letter is gone from the word

parts.note: a gallows is the structure from which people are hanged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the hook of a coat hanger has broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanger' suggests a coat hanger, but it is the gallows; 'top of' and 'is missing' together lose its G.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone in is to admit them, so allows and admits are synonyms.

clue.text: "Bond without Girl" we'll have to gainsay

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word for bond goes round the girl

parts.note: a bond is a binding agreement, a contract
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A film title, 'Bond without Girl', is something fans would have to deny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' evokes 007 and his girls; it is just a contract. 'Without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or speak against, which is what it means to contradict.

clue.text: All over a dish

parts.note: something all over is finished, in the past

explanation.surface: A plate of food covered right across.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian dish made from flour dough, such as spaghetti or penne.

clue.text: First child to cotton on gets a sweet

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to rumble someone is to cotton on to what they are up to

explanation.surface: The first child to understand something gets a candy as a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMBLE in its British informal sense means to see through or find out.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumble is a baked pudding of fruit topped with a crumbly mixture, and pudding is British for a sweet.

clue.text: Anxious teacher said to be taken in, tricked

indicators.note: the spoken sound goes inside the word for tricked

parts.note: to be tricked is to be conned

indicators.note: the word for teacher is spoken, giving a sound spelt differently

parts.note: a schoolboy addresses a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A worried teacher reportedly fell for a con and was fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like a synonym of tricked, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be concerned about something is to be worried or anxious about it.

clue.text: One prominent in the community

indicators.note: the letters stand out right in the middle of the following word

explanation.surface: A leading figure within the local neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one item counted as a whole.

clue.text: You'll be lost without these

parts.note: reads like praise of something indispensable, but literally describes the sense of direction whose absence leaves a person lost

explanation.surface: A slogan for an indispensable product.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose your bearings is to lose your sense of where you are, so without them you are lost.

clue.text: Got a rise, being promoted

definitions.meaning: raised to a higher rank or post

explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means lifted up physically and also raised in rank, matching both senses.

clue.text: Boy drops money in lake, contrariwise

indicators.note: with 'contrariwise', the money goes round the lake rather than the lake taking the money
reverses the stated container order, so the lake goes into the money

parts.note: coin is money
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A lad accidentally lets his cash fall into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, money goes in lake; 'contrariwise' flips it so L goes in COIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin is a common male first name, and crosswords routinely define a given name by example as simply boy.

clue.text: Combine to make Disney cat twitchy

indicators.note: a twitchy thing is jumpy and restless, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tease a cartoon feline from a famous studio until it becomes nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A combine is a group of businesses acting together, as is a syndicate.

clue.text: Endless walkabout: wave if one's not observing the rules

parts.note: read as 'endless walk' then 'about': walk without its last letter, turned round
a breaker is a large wave crashing on shore

explanation.surface: A never-ending stroll during which someone waves at people who flout regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'walkabout' into WALK + ABOUT: WAL (walk endless) reversed by 'about' gives LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker is a person who disobeys the rules of society.

clue.text: A month back, penniless in old money

indicators.note: without P, the abbreviation for a penny
the month is written backwards

parts.note: April is a month

explanation.surface: Thirty days ago someone was broke, counting only obsolete currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The lira was the currency of Italy before the euro replaced it, so it is old money.

clue.text: Joker, one who's almost a fibber, admits gravity of heartburn

parts.note: a joker is a playing card, and also a card is a joker or wag
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the shortened phrase lets the letter for gravity in
the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: a fibber is a liar
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A comedian, nearly a liar, confesses how serious his indigestion is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' seems to mean seriousness; it is G. 'Card' means a joker in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardialgia is the medical term for pain in the region of the heart, a technical name for heartburn.

clue.text: Straighten out daughter I roused by point of view

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
sent in the slang sense of excited or thrilled
an angle is a perspective or point of view

explanation.surface: Correct my daughter: I was angered by her opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To disentangle is to free from knots or confusion, to straighten out.

clue.text: 24, perhaps, catches sight of chap who's about right

indicators.note: the pair of words goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to spot is to catch sight of
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow spots a man who is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is BLUE: a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University is awarded a blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue is a sportsman who has competed for Oxford or Cambridge, so 24 is an example.

clue.text: Encounter animal first — a scrap in the air?

indicators.note: the animal is placed at the front

parts.note: a dog is an animal
an encounter can be a battle or fight

explanation.surface: Meet a beast first, then a brawl in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogfight is close combat between fighter aircraft, literally a scrap in the air.

clue.text: Tapioca he exchanged, missing nothing, for a plant

indicators.note: the letters are swapped round into a new order
the letter for nothing is left out of the pool

parts.note: O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man swaps his milk pudding for a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatica is a genus of woodland plants with liver-shaped leaves, related to the anemone.

clue.text: Vowed record improperly packed

indicators.note: the letters are put together in the wrong way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A vow was written down incorrectly and stuffed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcrowded means filled with too many people, packed.

clue.text: State car seen in Italian town

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: An official vehicle spotted in a town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a resort town on the Adriatic coast of Italy.

clue.text: Man in first with bidding

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the word for first

parts.note: the best is first
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man was the first to follow orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction, as in at someone's bidding.

clue.text: Languish beside Old Glory?

definitions.meaning: to weaken or tire, to droop
the nickname for the US stars and stripes, an example of a national banner

explanation.definitionFit: Flag means to tire and also a banner, Old Glory being the American one.

clue.text: Silver ore is mixed in the paste

indicators.note: the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Precious ore is combined into a paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephanite is a mineral, a silver antimony sulphide mined as an ore of silver.

clue.text: Accommodate either way

indicators.note: the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Give someone a bed for the night, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up is to give them a place to stay, to accommodate them.

clue.text: Chilly 15?

definitions.meaning: cold enough to turn the skin a cold colour
a sportsman of Oxford or Cambridge who has represented the university

explanation.walkthrough: 15 is SPORTSMAN: at Oxford and Cambridge, a blue is awarded for competing against the other university.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue describes skin made cold by chill and also a university sportsman, linked to 15.

clue.text: Nearly overact after bird set about one — a diving bird

indicators.note: the shortened word follows the bird
the bird is placed around the numeral for one

parts.note: a gull is a seabird
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: to emote is to overact

explanation.surface: Almost hamming it up after a bird attacked someone; it was a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' looks like attacked; it is the container signal round I.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that dives for fish.

clue.text: Semblance of fellows, so-called

indicators.note: the word for fellows is called out, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: fellows are guys

explanation.surface: Something resembling a group of men, as they are named.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or semblance, often a false one.

clue.text: Some jazz a German offers in part payment

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz, one kind of jazz
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A German musician offers to play some jazz as partial payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item given in part payment for a new one.

clue.text: Thespian is taking part as keyboard exponent

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow, taken out of them

explanation.surface: An actor is cast in the role of a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is someone who plays the piano, an exponent of the keyboard.
